recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的紅血球中央有一顆單一、小而圓、深紫色的緻密包涵體（Howell-Jolly body）；這顆紅血球本身略帶藍灰色（多染性）。
features: Single small (~1 µm), round, dense, dark purple inclusion within a red cell
Inclusion is solitary and sharply defined, not refractile
Host cell slightly larger with bluish-gray (polychromatophilic) tint and no central pallor
Another polychromatophilic red cell in the lower field
Background red cells normochromic without other inclusions; rare platelet
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic, normochromic red cells with occasional polychromatophilic cells. One polychromatophilic red cell (arrow) contains a single small, round, densely basophilic inclusion consistent with a Howell-Jolly body. No basophilic stippling, Pappenheimer body clusters, or intraerythrocytic parasites are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with Howell-Jolly body formation, which suggests hyposplenism or asplenia, or less often megaloblastic or dyserythropoietic states, in the appropriate clinical context.

ddx.vs: Pappenheimer bodies are multiple, smaller, irregular granules clustered at the cell periphery and are Prussian blue positive, whereas a Howell-Jolly body is a single larger round dot.
An overlying platelet is larger, granular pink-purple, often has a clear halo, and lies in a different focal plane.
A Plasmodium ring has a thin blue cytoplasmic ring attached to the chromatin dot, not a solid dot alone.
Stippling consists of numerous fine punctate granules distributed throughout the red cell rather than one discrete inclusion.
